international.headline: Paris hosts the first International Space Summit
facts: The first International Space Summit was held at the Grand Palais in Paris on September 9–10, 2026, under the theme “Coming together to take action for the planet.”
The summit was convened at the invitation of French President Emmanuel Macron; astronaut Thomas Pesquet and entrepreneur Hélène Huby served as Special Envoys.
Around 120 foreign delegations attended, alongside representatives of space agencies including NASA, ESA and CNSA, international organisations, scientists and private-sector leaders.
Discussions addressed space infrastructure and Earth observation for environmental protection, orbital sustainability and safety, responsible governance and equitable access to space technologies.
The European Space Agency was established in 1975 and is headquartered in Paris, France.
international.summary: The summit considered how international space cooperation can support environmental action and responsible use of space.
international.staticLink: The notes give Paris as the headquarters of the European Space Agency.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The inaugural International Space Summit was held in Paris on September 9–10, 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of space-based Earth observation and international governance in addressing global environmental challenges.

international.canonicalTopic: 9th ASEAN–India Agriculture and Forestry Ministers’ Meeting
international.headline: ASEAN–India agriculture and forestry ministers meet in New Delhi
facts: The 9th ASEAN–India Ministerial Meeting on Agriculture and Forestry (AIMMAF) was held in New Delhi on September 9, 2026.
It was co-chaired by Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Philippine Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel.

The meeting adopted “ASEAN 2045: Our Shared Future” and the “ASEAN Food, Agriculture and Forestry Sectoral Plan 2026–2030,” focused on resilient development, food security and environmental protection.
The ASEAN–India Medium-Term Plan of Action 2026–30 includes joint research, digital technology exchange, policy dialogue and farmer exchange programmes.
Cooperation priorities include AI-based digital agriculture, low-emission rice cultivation, water productivity, soil health, circular bioeconomy and sustainable value chains.
The 10th ASEAN–India Working Group on Agriculture and Forestry finalised technical recommendations the day before the ministerial meeting.
The notes report ASEAN–India merchandise trade of USD 128 billion in 2025–26.
ASEAN was established on August 8, 1967, and is headquartered in Jakarta; the notes list 11 members and Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn.
international.summary: The ministerial meeting adopted regional frameworks and an action plan for agriculture and forestry cooperation, including priorities in digital agriculture and sustainable production.
international.staticLink: ASEAN–India relations developed from a Sectoral Dialogue Partnership in 1992 to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2022.
international.prelimsTakeaway: AIMMAF is the ministerial platform for ASEAN–India cooperation in agriculture and forestry; the meeting was co-chaired by Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Francisco P. Tiu Laurel.
international.mainsAngle: Analyse how India–ASEAN cooperation in agricultural technology, low-emission cultivation and resilient value chains can support food security.

national.canonicalTopic: Inter-State Council Order amended for meetings during President’s Rule
national.headline: Governors and Delhi’s Lieutenant Governor to be invited to Inter-State Council meetings in specified circumstances
facts: President Droupadi Murmu amended the Inter-State Council Order, 1990 through the Inter-State Council (Amendment) Order, 2026; the Ministry of Home Affairs notified it on September 9, 2026, and it took effect upon publication.
The amendment was issued under Article 263 of the Constitution.

When President’s Rule under Article 356 applies in a State, that State’s Governor will be invited to an Inter-State Council meeting; when an order under Article 239AB applies in the National Capital Territory of Delhi, the Lieutenant Governor will be invited.
The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission; the Prime Minister chairs it and its Secretariat is under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
national.summary: The amended Inter-State Council Order provides for inviting the relevant Governor or Delhi Lieutenant Governor to Council meetings in the specified constitutional situations.
national.staticLink: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council; Article 356 concerns President’s Rule in a State and Article 239AB concerns failure of constitutional machinery in Delhi.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The amendment was made under Article 263 and notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs on September 9, 2026.
national.mainsAngle: The amendment connects intergovernmental coordination with constitutional arrangements during President’s Rule and specified conditions in Delhi.

sources.title: Governors/Lieutenant Governors to Attend Inter-State Council Meetings during President’s Rule

national.notes:

- **Amended by:** **President Droupadi Murmu**

- **Status:** **Approved**; effective upon publication
- **Constitutional basis:** **Article 263**

# 2. Invitation circumstances
| Situation | Invitee | Constitutional provision |
|---|---|---|
| **President’s Rule** in a **State** | Governor of that **State** | **Article 356** |
| Order applies in the **National Capital Territory of Delhi** | **Lieutenant Governor** of **Delhi** | **Article 239AB** |

# 3. Inter-State Council background

- **Secretariat:** **Ministry of Home Affairs**

> Exam angle: Match the amendment’s invitation provisions with **Articles 356 and 239AB**, and its constitutional basis with **Article 263**.

national.headline: Home Ministry proposes a special constitutional provision for Ladakh under Article 371
facts: At a meeting in New Delhi on 2026-09-09, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs proposed a special constitutional provision for Ladakh under Article 371, titled “Chapter K.”
The proposal includes a directly elected governing body for the Union Territory and safeguards concerning land, culture, language, forests and the environment, linked to Article 240.
Article 371 is in Part XXI; the notes cite Articles 371A for Nagaland, 371B for Assam, 371C for Manipur, 371D for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and 371G for Mizoram.
Representatives including the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance sought safeguards and reiterated demands for full statehood and Sixth Schedule protection for tribal areas.
The Sixth Schedule provides for Autonomous District Councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram and is based on Articles 244(2) and 275(1).
Ladakh became a Union Territory on 2019-10-31 after the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir.
national.summary: The Union Home Ministry proposed a special constitutional arrangement for Ladakh, including an elected governing body and protections for land, culture and the environment. The proposal is linked to Article 240 and comes amid demands for safeguards and Sixth Schedule protection.
national.staticLink: Constitution of India: Part XXI, Articles 240 and 371; Sixth Schedule: Articles 244(2) and 275(1).
national.prelimsTakeaway: The proposal is for Ladakh; Article 371 provisions are in Part XXI, while the Sixth Schedule provides for Autonomous District and Regional Councils.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how constitutional safeguards and autonomous institutions can address regional aspirations while protecting tribal land, culture and environment.
